macro-calculator.assumptionNote: Targets use the Mifflin-St Jeor equation and standard sport-nutrition protein ranges - good estimates, not medical prescriptions.
benefits: Turns vague diet advice into exact daily numbers.
Protects muscle while losing fat by setting protein first.
Adjusts calories to your goal instead of a one-size-fits-all number.
Makes tracking apps easier: you know your three numbers before you log a single meal.

faqs.a: About 0.8 g per kg covers a sedentary person. Active people do better at 1.2-1.6 g, and people dieting or building muscle at 1.6-2.2 g. This calculator sets 1.6-2.0 g by goal.
faqs.q: How much protein do I really need?

faqs.a: Protein 4 kcal/g, carbs 4 kcal/g, fat 9 kcal/g. Alcohol is 7 kcal/g. These are Atwater factors - averages from lab measurements.
faqs.q: How many calories are in each macro?

faqs.a: Fat is essential: hormones, brain, and vitamin absorption all need it. Dropping below about 0.5 g per kg risks hormone problems. Carbs fuel hard training; cut those before fat.
faqs.q: Should I cut carbs or fat to lose weight?

faqs.a: No. Percentages hide the absolute grams your muscles need. A 60 kg dieter and a 100 kg lifter can share 25% protein and need completely different grams. Grams first, always.
Yes - scale them to the calories you actually eat. The gram targets stay the same; just know the kcal totals will not match the target until you eat at the target.
faqs.q: Can I use these macros on rest days?

faqs.a: Re-check monthly, or after a 2-3 kg weight change. As you get lighter you need fewer calories; as you get more muscular you need more protein.

macro-calculator.formula:
Mifflin-St Jeor BMR:
Men: 10 x W(kg) + 6.25 x H(cm) - 5 x Age + 5
Women: 10 x W(kg) + 6.25 x H(cm) - 5 x Age - 161

TDEE = BMR x activity (1.2 - 1.9)
Goal: lose -400 kcal, maintain +/-0, gain +300 kcal

Protein: 2.0 / 1.8 / 1.6 g per kg (lose / maintain / gain)
Fat: 0.8 g per kg
Carbs: (target kcal - protein x 4 - fat x 9) / 4
howTo: Enter sex, age, height, and weight honestly - the BMR formula needs all four.
Pick the activity level closest to your real week, not your best week.
Choose your goal: lose fat, maintain, or gain muscle.
Your daily calorie target and protein/carb/fat grams appear instantly.
Re-check monthly or after a 2-3 kg change - your numbers move as your body does.
keyFacts: Macros = protein, carbs, fat: the three calorie-containing nutrients.
Protein has 4 kcal per gram, carbs 4, fat 9. That is why fat portions must stay small.
This calculator sets protein first (1.6-2.0 g/kg by goal), then fat (0.8 g/kg), then fills carbs.
BMR comes from the Mifflin-St Jeor equation - the most validated formula for adults.
TDEE multiplies BMR by activity: 1.2 sedentary to 1.9 very active.
Losing fat needs about a 400 kcal daily deficit; gaining muscle about a 300 kcal surplus.

limitations: Estimates, not prescriptions - a dietitian personalizes for health conditions.
Activity multipliers are rough; desk workers who train hard often land between levels.
Does not account for metabolic adaptation after long diets.
Not for children, pregnant women, or people with eating disorders - seek professional guidance.

macro-calculator.quickAnswer: For a 30-year-old man, 175 cm, 80 kg, moderately active, maintaining: BMR is about 1,749 kcal, TDEE about 2,711 kcal. That gives roughly 144 g protein, 390 g carbs, and 64 g fat per day - protein first (1.8 g/kg), fat at 0.8 g/kg, and carbs filling the rest.
